Currently `OptimismMintableERC721Factory` is using a constructor and is initialized by encoding the constructor in [`L2Genesis.s.sol:363-382`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/3235773247caa4db47f8dcc695fddfce6d40b171/packages/contracts-bedrock/scripts/L2Genesis.s.sol#L363).

topIssues.title: [L2CM] Reuse ProxyAdmin tests on L2ProxyAdmin for backwards compatibility
topIssues.author: aliersh
topIssues.body:
**FMA follow-up (FM3):** `L2ProxyAdmin` replaces the existing `ProxyAdmin` predeploy. Other L2 contracts (`FeeVault`, `L1Withdrawer`, `FeeSplitter`) call `owner()` on it for access control. We need to verify that all existing `ProxyAdmin` functionality still works on `L2ProxyAdmin`.

Rather than writing a differential test from scratch, reuse the existing `ProxyAdmin.t.sol` ERC1967 test paths against `L2ProxyAdmin`. This proves backwards compatibility without duplicating test logic.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Existing `ProxyAdmin.t.sol` ERC1967 tests run successfully against `L2ProxyAdmin`
- Core functions verified: `owner()`, `upgrade()`, `upgradeAndCall()`, `changeProxyAdmin()`, `getProxyImplementation()`, `getProxyAdmin()`

### References

- [L2CM FMA — FM3: L2ProxyAdmin Backwards Compatibility Break](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/security/fma-l2cm.md)
- Existing tests: `packages/contracts-bedrock/test/universal/ProxyAdmin.t.sol`

topIssues.title: [L2CM] Investigate automated enforcement: no storage variables in L2ContractsManager
topIssues.author: aliersh
topIssues.body:
**FMA follow-up (FM2):** `L2ContractsManager` executes via `DELEGATECALL` in the `L2ProxyAdmin`'s storage context. If it declares storage variables, they would collide with `ProxyAdmin` slots (e.g., `_owner`), potentially locking out admin access permanently.

The convention is already followed (PR #19111 uses only immutables), but there is no automated enforcement. Investigate adding a Semgrep rule or Foundry test that blocks `L2ContractsManager` from declaring storage variables.

**Note:** This is non-blocking. OPCM operates without this enforcement and is doing fine. But it's worth investigating as a safety net.

### Acceptance Criteria

- Investigation complete: determine whether a Semgrep rule, Foundry test, or other mechanism is feasible
- If feasible: implement the enforcement

### References

- [L2CM FMA — FM2: Storage Layout Corruption](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/security/fma-l2cm.md)

topIssues.title: [L2CM] Add ProxyAdminOwnedBase access control to predeploy initialize() functions
topIssues.author: aliersh
topIssues.body:
**FMA follow-up (FM1):** As identified in the [L2CM FMA](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/security/fma-l2cm.md), the L2CM upgrade mechanism clears the `initialized` slot and re-calls `initialize()` on predeploy proxies. If `initialize()` is open to anyone post-upgrade, an attacker could front-run or re-initialize with malicious parameters.

All predeploy contracts that have an `initialize()` function should use [`ProxyAdminOwnedBase._assertOnlyProxyAdminOrProxyAdminOwner()`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/develop/packages/contracts-bedrock/src/L1/ProxyAdminOwnedBase.sol#L101) to restrict who can call `initialize()`.

### Acceptance Criteria

- All proxied L2 predeploy `initialize()` functions are protected with `ProxyAdminOwnedBase` access control
- Tests verify that `initialize()` reverts when called by unauthorized addresses

### References

- [L2CM FMA — FM1: Re-initialization State Corruption](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/design-docs/blob/main/security/fma-l2cm.md)

topPRs.author: 0xiamflux
topPRs.body:
## Overview
Adds the L2ContractsManager contract that handles upgrades of L2 predeploys via DELEGATECALL from ProxyAdmin. It's based on the L2ContractsManager specs [here](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/884).
                                                                                                                                                                                                
  - Implements clear-and-reinitialize pattern using StorageSetter for initializable contracts                                                                                                     
  - Preserves network-specific configuration by reading from existing predeploys before upgrade                                                                                                   
  - Handles Custom Gas Token conditional upgrades (L1BlockCGT, L2ToL1MessagePasserCGT, LiquidityController, NativeAssetLiquidity).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            
                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  Note: Feature flag handling beyond Custom Gas Token is deferred to future work.

topPRs.title: pure: add pure derivation pipeline in op-core/pure
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- Adds `op-core/pure/` package implementing a pure function derivation pipeline
- `PureDerive()` takes L1 data + safe head state, returns derived L2 payload attributes — no I/O, no L2 state reads
- Post-Holocene only, with protocol modification: no overlapping span batches (eliminates L2 fetcher dependency)

## Design

Single pure function that loops over L1 blocks sequentially:
1. Apply system config updates from L1 receipts
2. Parse frames from batcher transactions
3. Assemble channels (Holocene single-channel strict-order model)
4. Decode and validate batches
5. Build payload attributes (L1 info deposit + user deposits + batch txs)
6. Generate empty batches when sequencer window expires

Reuses existing pure functions from `op-node/rollup/derive/` (frame parsing, channel assembly, batch decoding, deposit encoding, L1 block info). Fresh implementation for the orchestration layer.

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `types.go` | L1Input, DerivedBlock, l2Cursor, BlockInfo adapter |
| `channels.go` | Holocene single-channel assembler |
| `batches.go` | Batch decoding, validation, empty batch generation |
| `attributes.go` | PayloadAttributes assembly |
| `derive.go` | `PureDerive()` entry point |
| `helpers_test.go` | Shared test utilities |

## Test plan

- [x] 31 unit tests covering all pipeline stages
- [x] Channel assembly: single-frame, multi-frame, new channel discards old, timeout, out-of-order
- [x] Batch validation: correct timestamp, wrong timestamp, epoch range, overlap rejection
- [x] Empty batch generation: window expiry detection, correct epoch advancement
- [x] Attributes assembly: epoch boundaries, same epoch, Holocene-specific fields
- [x] End-to-end: single batch, empty epochs, multiple channels/epochs, channel timeout, invalid batch skip
- [ ] Differential test against existing pipeline (follow-up)

topPRs.title: refactor(op-devstack): migrate Orchestrator to unified Registry (Phase 4)
topPRs.author: teddyknox
topPRs.body:
This PR completes Phase 4 of the ID type system refactor by migrating the Orchestrator from 15 separate `locks.RWMap` registry fields to a single unified `*stack.Registry`.

**Key changes:**
- Replace 15 typed registry fields (`l1ELs`, `l2CLs`, `batchers`, etc.) with single `registry *stack.Registry`
- Update `GetL2EL` to use `FindL2ELCapableByKey` for polymorphic lookups across L2ELNode, RollupBoostNode, and OPRBuilderNode
- Update `Hydrate` method to iterate components by kind with explicit ordering
- Update all `ControlPlane` methods to use registry lookups with type assertions
- Migrate ~24 files to use consistent `registry.Register()` and `registry.Get()` patterns

### Motivation

The previous Orchestrator maintained 15 separate `locks.RWMap` fields, each keyed by its own ID type:

```go
// Before: 15 separate registries
type Orchestrator struct {
    l1ELs           locks.RWMap[stack.L1ELNodeID, L1ELNode]
    l2CLs           locks.RWMap[stack.L2CLNodeID, L2CLNode]
    batchers        locks.RWMap[stack.L2BatcherID, *L2Batcher]
    rollupBoosts    locks.RWMap[stack.RollupBoostNodeID, *RollupBoostNode]
    // ... 11 more fields
}
```

This led to:
- Duplicate lookup logic across registries
- Complex polymorphic lookups (GetL2EL had to check 3 different maps)
- No unified way to query "all components on chain X"
- Adding new component types required adding new registry fields

### Solution

Consolidate all component storage into a single registry:

```go
// After: Single unified registry
type Orchestrator struct {
    registry *stack.Registry
}
```

The registry provides:
- Primary storage: `ComponentID -> component`
- Secondary index by kind: `ComponentKind -> []ComponentID`
- Secondary index by chain: `ChainID -> []ComponentID`

### Migration Patterns

**Registration:**
```go
// Before
orch.batchers.Set(batcherID, b)

// After
orch.registry.Register(stack.ConvertL2BatcherID(batcherID).ComponentID, b)
```

**Lookup:**
```go
// Before
batcher, ok := orch.batchers.Get(id)

// After
component, ok := orch.registry.Get(stack.ConvertL2BatcherID(id).ComponentID)
batcher := component.(*L2Batcher)
```

**Polymorphic Lookup (using Phase 3 capabilities):**
```go
// Before: 15 lines checking 3 maps
func (o *Orchestrator) GetL2EL(id stack.L2ELNodeID) (L2ELNode, bool) {
    if el, ok := o.l2ELs.Get(id); ok { return el, true }
    rbID := stack.NewRollupBoostNodeID(id.Key(), id.ChainID())
    if rb, ok := o.rollupBoosts.Get(rbID); ok { return rb, true }
    // ... check OPRBuilder too
}

// After: 5 lines with capability interface
func (o *Orchestrator) GetL2EL(id stack.L2ELNodeID) (L2ELNode, bool) {
    capable, ok := stack.FindL2ELCapableByKey(o.registry, id.Key(), id.ChainID())
    if !ok { return nil, false }
    if el, ok := capable.(L2ELNode); ok { return el, true }
    return nil, false
}
```

### Files Changed

| Category | Files |
|----------|-------|
| Core | `sysgo/orchestrator.go`, `sysgo/control_plane.go`, `sysgo/deployer.go` |
| L2 EL nodes | `sysgo/l2_el_opgeth.go`, `sysgo/l2_el_opreth.go`, `sysgo/l2_el_synctester.go`, `sysgo/rollup_boost.go`, `sysgo/op_rbuilder.go` |
| L2 CL nodes | `sysgo/l2_cl_opnode.go`, `sysgo/l2_cl_kona.go`, `sysgo/l2_cl_supernode.go`, `sysgo/l2_cl_p2p_util.go` |
| Services | `sysgo/l2_batcher.go`, `sysgo/l2_proposer.go`, `sysgo/l2_challenger.go`, `sysgo/faucet.go` |
| Infrastructure | `sysgo/supervisor.go`, `sysgo/supervisor_op.go`, `sysgo/supervisor_kona.go`, `sysgo/sync_tester.go`, `sysgo/test_sequencer.go` |
| Other | `sysgo/add_game_type.go`, `sysgo/l2_metrics_dashboard.go`, `sysgo/l2_network_superchain_registry.go` |

### Special Cases

**l2MetricsEndpoints**: This field stores Prometheus scrape targets, not components, so it remains separate. Changed from `locks.RWMap` to `map[string][]PrometheusMetricsTarget` with `sync.RWMutex`.

### Test Plan

- [x] All 54 stack tests pass
- [x] Polymorphic lookups work for RollupBoostNode and OPRBuilderNode
- [x] Hydrate correctly initializes components in dependency order
- [x] ControlPlane can start/stop all component types
- [x] Build compiles without errors

### Related

- Phase 1 PR: Unified ComponentID with generic wrappers
- Phase 2 PR: Unified Registry implementation
- Phase 3 PR: Capability interfaces (L2ELCapable)
- [Design document](https://www.notion.so/oplabs/Devstack-ID-Type-System-Refactor-2eef153ee1628048bb7ade1030fe6e9b)
